trust_decision.summary: A handler's exception text must not be placed in the gRPC status details sent to the client unless GRPC_NODE_DEBUG_SEND_ERROR_DETAILS is true (default false); the decision is implemented inline in the four handle* catch blocks in packages/grpc-js/src/server.ts, with the flag supplied by packages/grpc-js/src/environment.ts.

landing_point.why: The report says the server sends handler-thrown error messages to the client; the first and most obvious place is the try/catch around handler.func in handleUnary that builds details from (err as Error).message.

fix_sites.entry_point: Server.addService()/Server.register() unary handler, invoked synchronously at onReceiveHalfClose
Server.addService()/Server.register() client-streaming handler, invoked at onReceiveMetadata
Server.addService()/Server.register() server-streaming handler, invoked at onReceiveHalfClose
Server.addService()/Server.register() bidi-streaming handler, invoked at onReceiveMetadata
Module-level GRPC_NODE_DEBUG_SEND_ERROR_DETAILS constant (added next to packages/grpc-js/src/environment.ts:18-19), read by all four catches

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: packages/grpc-js/src/environment.ts:18-19 (the new default-off flag is appended here by fix.diff:26-27)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The env module is just plumbing, so redacting inline in server.ts satisfies the report; and any error the application itself hands to the respond callback or emits on the stream is the documented way to send a status, not an error 'thrown by a method handler', so it stays out (existing tests already require those details to pass through).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Statuses the application deliberately returns must still reach the client verbatim: cb({code, details}) and cb(new Error(msg)) on unary/client-stream, and stream.emit('error', {code, details, metadata}) / stream.emit('error', new Error(msg)) on server-stream/bidi, including UTF-8 and comma-containing details and non-standard codes. A blanket redaction of every error-derived details string breaks all of these.

O6_input_shapes: synchronously thrown Error from a unary, client-stream, server-stream or bidi handler
synchronously thrown non-Error value (string/object), where .message is undefined
explicit {code, details} status carried on the thrown/returned error (redacted by the fix even when details is safe)
async handler rejection after an await (not caught by any of the four try/catch blocks; no status is sent)
error passed to the response callback, cb(err), for unary and client-stream (not handled by the fix)
error emitted on the server stream or passed to stream.destroy(err) for server-stream and bidi (not handled by the fix)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Unary and client-streaming handler passes an Error to the response callback (cb(err)); respond() calls serverErrorToStatus, which copies error.message into status details and sends it
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names errors thrown by handlers; cb(new Error(...)) is the application explicitly choosing to report a status through the documented API, and packages/grpc-js/test/test-server-errors.ts:759-770 asserts the message is transmitted

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Server-streaming and bidi handler emits 'error' (or stream.destroy(err)); the stream listener stores serverErrorToStatus(err) as pendingStatus and _final sends its details
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Aborting a streaming RPC with stream.emit('error', status) is the documented pattern for streams (there is no throwing equivalent after the handler returns), so it reads as a deliberate status rather than a leaked exception

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The handler's user-supplied response serializer throws; the interceptor sends 'Error serializing response: ' plus the raw error message
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: That is the serializer (proto-loader/protobuf code), not the method handler; existing tests only assert the INTERNAL code and never the details (packages/grpc-js/test/test-server-errors.ts:259-288)
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different module from the report's landing point (server-interceptors.ts vs server.ts)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The handler's user-supplied request deserializer throws; the interceptor sends 'Error deserializing request: ' plus the raw error message
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Deserialization belongs to the proto-loader/serializer layer, not to the handler the advisory talks about
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different module from the report's landing point (server-interceptors.ts vs server.ts)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: serverErrorToStatus also honours a caller-supplied string details on any status object (err.details) even when code is a non-standard integer, so the application text wins over the message fallback
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: An explicit details field is an intentional status field, not an incidental error message, so it is arguably outside a rule aimed at thrown exceptions

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second error-to-status converter (e.g. for an async/promise handler form or a new stream wrapper) that repeats the 'details: error.message' line
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the single place the codebase converts an Error into a status object; any new call shape added by a maintainer would naturally reuse it rather than go through the inline catch blocks

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third sendStatus site that embeds an application-supplied callback's error message (serialize, write, metadata)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The serialize and write failure handlers already exist side by side and both interpolate getErrorMessage(e); adding a metadata/header failure handler in the same shape is a natural next edit

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A new handler type branch (_runHandlerForCall) whose catch reports handler error text
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Handler types are dispatched by name in _runHandlerForCall and every unknown type currently produces its own sendStatus; a maintainer adding a handler kind would add the branch here

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A server interceptor wrapper in another package that rewrites or forwards handler error details
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: XdsServer extends Server and installs its own ServerInterceptors that already call call.sendStatus; a redaction interceptor or an error-forwarding filter is a plausible addition in that package

O9_family: information exposure through error/status message (CWE-550, server-generated error message carrying sensitive application detail)

O10_build.toolchain: npm, TypeScript 5.x (tsc -p .), gulp + mocha for tests, proto-loader-gen-types codegen run by pretest
O10_build.project_tests: packages/grpc-js/test/test-server-errors.ts (status code/details for unary, client-stream, server-stream and bidi, plus serialization failures), packages/grpc-js/test/test-server.ts (unimplemented-method details), packages/grpc-js/test/test-server-interceptors.ts; all bind in-process localhost servers, run with npm test (gulp test) in packages/grpc-js

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Redact inside serverErrorToStatus (or every sendStatus that builds details from an error), which passes the thrown-error test but silently drops the application's deliberate {code, details} statuses and breaks test-server-errors.ts

out_of_scope_notes: packages/grpc-js-xds/src/server.ts was checked only for a second server implementation reaching this sink; XdsServer extends Server and does not alter handler error dispatch, and its own sendStatus calls carry internal routing errors.
